title: Barbecue Pulled Chicken Sandwiches with Apple Slaw
changes_from_base: Thighs are pressure-cooked for 6 minutes in a tangy ketchup, Worcestershire and mustard barbecue sauce, mashed into shreds, then sautéed until a little caramelised and served with a crunchy apple, cabbage and shallot slaw.
summary: Tender pulled chicken cooked in a pressure cooker with warm spices and a tangy barbecue sauce, piled high with a crisp, fresh apple and cabbage slaw.
equipment: electric pressure cooker (such as an Instant Pot)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
tart green apple (such as Granny Smith), cored and cut into thin matchsticks
fine sea salt or table salt
brioche burger buns, split and toasted if you like

steps.title: Slaw
steps.text: Whisk together 1½ tbsp cider vinegar, 1 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tsp light brown sugar and 1 tsp fine salt in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves. Toss in 140 g shredded green cabbage, a tart green apple cut into matchsticks, and a sliced shallot, then set aside.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Combine 180 ml ketchup, 2 tbsp light brown sugar, 1½ tbsp cider vinegar, 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tsp Dijon mustard and 2 tsp hot sauce in a small bowl and set aside.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in the pressure cooker on its highest sauté setting and soften 1 small chopped onion for 3-5 minutes. Stir in 2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tsp chilli powder, ¾ tsp fine salt and ½ tsp cayenne pepper for 30 seconds to bloom the spices.

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Add 120 ml of the sauce and 900 g chicken thighs to the cooker and mix to coat everything evenly in a single layer. Lock the lid, close the valve and cook at high pressure for 6 minutes, then quick-release the pressure, opening the lid away from you.

steps.title: Shred
steps.text: Reserve 120 ml of the cooking liquid from the pot and keep 60 ml of it to one side; discard the remainder. Shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces using 2 forks directly in the pot and check that the thickest part reaches 74 °C.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: Switch the cooker back to sauté and simmer the chicken, scraping the bottom as it cooks, for 6-8 minutes until all the liquid has evaporated and a little browning forms on the base of the pot.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Remove from the heat and stir in the reserved 60 ml of cooking liquid and a further 60 ml of the sauce. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the pulled chicken onto split brioche buns, spoon more sauce over the top, add a generous heap of apple and cabbage slaw and top with the bun lids. For smaller portions, use slider buns instead.

tips: Make the slaw just before serving so the apple and cabbage stay crisp and fresh-tasting alongside the warm, saucy chicken.
The cooking liquid reduces down as the chicken cooks; keeping some back lets you add moisture and richness at the end without the finished dish being soggy.
Worcestershire sauce usually contains anchovy, so check the label if you need the sauce fish-free.
storage: Best eaten straight away while the chicken is warm and the slaw is still crisp. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
